summary:
The rule values are right. I found no wrong tax bracket, CPF rate or ceiling, relief amount or cap for income years 2025, 2026 or 2027, and no blocker. For a Citizen or PR under 55 using SRS and a top-up to their own CPF, the tool is safe to sell once the wording fixes below are made.

It is not yet safe for three groups, because the model assumes things it cannot know and says too little about them:

1. **Foreigners.** The tool shows them the same "S$40,000 a year comes out tax-free" promise as a citizen. That only holds for someone who is tax resident when they withdraw. A foreigner who leaves pays at least 7.5% of every SRS dollar withdrawn, or at least 20% if they withdraw early. On the default setting, part of the recommended S$35,700 loses money.
2. **People topping up parents.** The first S$2,000 a year to a parent on the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme earns no relief. The tool counts it as relief and has no way to enter it.
3. **People aged 55 and over.** The CPF Board accepts top-ups that earn no relief, and the plan includes S$8,000 by default with only an info-level note.

Three more material gaps:
- The tool never says that "voluntary contributions to all three CPF accounts" earn no relief.
- It never says what makes someone a tax resident, and gives no warning for a foreigner who worked under 183 days.
- The paid workbook leaves out most of the "before you transfer" facts the free web page has, including that half of SRS withdrawals are taxed later.

The dollar examples come from running the engine on test profiles; the script is at .tmp/final-review/practitioner-cases.ts. Official pages could not be opened, so "verified-by-search" means search extracts of IRAS and CPF Board pages.

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:424-431 ("Tax later" row), 408-411, 66-71; src/engine/warnings.ts:221-235 (FOREIGNER_NO_CPF); src/web/state.ts:25 (7% default for every residency); workbook/sheets/planner.ts:314; workbook/sheets/working.ts:792-798; SPEC.md section 5.4 line 179
findings.claim_or_behaviour: A user who picks Foreigner gets the same SRS facts as a citizen: "Half of each withdrawal is taxable. You can spread withdrawals over up to 10 years; with no other income, S$40,000 a year comes out tax-free." The only foreigner-specific message is "You can put up to S$35,700 a year into SRS." The default "Worth it (7%+)" then fills SRS down through the 7% bracket. Nothing mentions leaving Singapore or the 10-year rule for foreigners.
findings.what_is_true: The S$40,000 tax-free result needs the person to be a Singapore tax resident in the year of withdrawal. For foreigners and PRs the SRS bank withholds 24% of the taxable amount. A non-resident's final tax is 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher (IRAS example: S$300,000 withdrawn, S$150,000 taxable, S$22,500 tax). So a non-resident pays at least 7.5% of a withdrawal at retirement age or under the foreigners' concession (not a citizen or PR for 10 years, account held 10 years from first contribution, one full withdrawal, 50% taxable, no penalty). An earlier withdrawal costs at least 20% (15% on the whole amount plus the 5% penalty). Sources: IRAS, "Tax on SRS withdrawals" (iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals) and IRAS, "Withdrawal from SRS account (foreigners/PRs): tax obligations" and "Calculating withholding tax" (iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/withdrawal-from-supplementary-retirement-scheme-(srs)-account-(foreigners-prs)/). Verified this audit from search extracts of those pages, returned consistently by two searches.
findings.consequence: Engine run: foreigner aged 32 on S$7,000 a month plus S$7,000 bonus. The tool recommends S$35,700 into SRS and says it saves S$2,949 (S$10,000 at 11.5%, S$25,700 at 7%). If she later withdraws as a non-resident after 10 years, the tax is at least S$2,677.50, leaving S$271.50. The S$25,700 in the 7% rung loses money (S$1,799 saved, at least S$1,927.50 paid). If she leaves within 10 years and closes the account, it costs at least S$7,140, a net loss of about S$4,190. On S$9,000 a month plus S$12,000 bonus the tool shows S$4,105.50 saved; an early exit costs at least S$7,140. PRs and citizens who retire abroad face the same non-resident rule.
findings.suggested_fix: When residency is Foreigner: (1) show a caution beside the recommendation and in the workbook's "Things to check": "If you may leave Singapore: a non-resident has no tax-free band on SRS withdrawals. IRAS taxes the taxable part at 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher, and the bank withholds 24% first. That is at least 7.5% of what you take out at retirement age or under the 10-year rule for foreigners, and at least 20% if you take it out sooner (tax on the full amount plus the 5% penalty)." (2) Replace the "Tax later" cell for foreigners with the same facts. (3) For foreigners, default the minimum saving to the 11.5% rung instead of 7%. Show a one-line version to PRs.

findings.where: SPEC.md section 6.3 line 331 and section 5.6 lines 204-205; src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:407-428; src/web/text.ts:444-451, 487, 489-492, 518; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:290, 345-355; workbook/sheets/start.ts:108
findings.claim_or_behaviour: With the family top-up switched on, every dollar up to S$8,000 is counted as relief. The only inputs are the on/off box and "Most I would give (optional)". The matching-grant rule appears only as a general line with no amount: "A top-up that attracts a government matching grant earns no tax relief."
findings.what_is_true: Since 1 January 2025 the part of a cash top-up that attracts the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme grant earns no relief. The grant matches the first S$2,000 a year per eligible member (S$20,000 lifetime). Eligible members are Singapore Citizens aged 55 or over with retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum (S$110,200 in 2026), average monthly income of S$4,000 or less and modest property. Since 1 January 2026 the same applies to the Matched MediSave Scheme, which matches up to S$1,000 a year for eligible citizens aged 55 to 70. Amounts beyond the matched part still earn relief. Sources: CPF Board, "Matching grant for retirement" and "Matched Retirement Savings Scheme: what you need to know" (cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/government-support/matching-grant-for-retirement); IRAS, "CPF Cash Top-up Relief". Verified this audit from search extracts.
findings.consequence: The opening example person (35, S$135,000 a year) switches on only the family top-up. The tool says S$8,000 saves S$920. If it goes to one eligible parent, only S$6,000 earns relief (S$690). Split between two eligible parents, S$4,000 earns relief (S$460). S$2,000 each to four eligible parents and in-laws earns none. Retired parents with low balances are the usual recipients and are often on the scheme.
findings.suggested_fix: Best: add an optional field under the family box, "How much of this will the Government match? (S$2,000 a year per parent on the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, S$1,000 for MediSave under the Matched MediSave Scheme)", and leave that amount out of the relief. Minimum, with no model change: put the numbers in the family box hint, the caution list and the workbook note at planner.ts:346: "If your parent gets the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme grant, the first S$2,000 topped up for them each year is matched and earns you no tax relief (S$1,000 for MediSave under the Matched MediSave Scheme). Only top-ups beyond that count towards your S$8,000. Ask them to check their CPF Retirement Dashboard."

findings.where: src/engine/warnings.ts:251-265 (AGE_55_PLUS_TOPUP, severity info); SPEC.md section 6.11 line 495 and Appendix A.2; src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:391-404; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:330-336; workbook/sheets/working.ts:805-810
findings.claim_or_behaviour: For someone aged 55 or over the plan still includes S$8,000 "into your CPF" by default. The only signal is an info-level note lower on the page: "From age 55, cash top-ups go to your Retirement Account and earn tax relief only up to the Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400 in 2026). Check your balance and enter the room you have left." The room field is optional, with placeholder "Not sure" and hint "Leave empty if the limits are far off."
findings.what_is_true: Relief on Retirement Account top-ups stops at the current year's Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400 for 2026), but the CPF Board accepts cash up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (S$440,800). Under 55, the Board will not accept a top-up above the Full Retirement Sum; from 55 it will, so money can go in with no relief. Someone who turns 55 this year and sets aside the full sum has no relief room at all that year (my inference from the rule; IRAS's own example gives S$0 relief when the account is at the Full Retirement Sum). The test is not the account balance: CPF's figure leaves out interest and government grants. The CPF Retirement Dashboard shows the remaining tax relief for the year. Sources: IRAS, "CPF Cash Top-up Relief"; CPF Board, "Top up to enjoy higher retirement payouts" (cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/top-up-to-enjoy-higher-retirement-payouts). Verified this audit from search extracts.
findings.consequence: Engine run: a citizen who turned 55 in March 2026, S$12,000 a month plus S$24,000 bonus, S$5,000 other reliefs. The plan is S$15,300 SRS plus S$8,000 CPF, "saves S$3,315.10". If his Retirement Account already holds the Full Retirement Sum, the S$8,000 earns nothing. The true saving is S$2,295, so S$1,020.10 is overstated and S$8,000 is in the Retirement Account for good.
findings.suggested_fix: For age 55 and over, do not assume unlimited room: treat a blank room field as S$0 (or require it) and say so in the headline. Raise AGE_55_PLUS_TOPUP to caution and show it under the headline. Reword it: "From 55 the CPF Board accepts top-ups up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum, but only the part up to the Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400 in 2026) earns tax relief. Log in to CPF, open the Retirement Dashboard and enter the tax relief you can still get this year. If you turned 55 this year and set aside the full sum, that is S$0."

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:37-41 and 122-127 (headline "into your CPF"), 444-451 ("No relief for"); src/engine/warnings.ts:213-216; SPEC.md section 5.2 line 137 and section 5.4 line 175; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:282-283, 324-326
findings.claim_or_behaviour: The plan says "Put S$8,000 into your CPF". "No relief for" lists only "CPF-to-CPF transfers, top-ups that attract a matching grant ... and amounts above the limits." Voluntary contributions are mentioned once, in a warning that only appears when the CPF override is too high: "Voluntary contributions do not earn CPF relief."
findings.what_is_true: The CPF Board offers three look-alike ways to put cash in: a retirement top-up to the Special or Retirement Account, a MediSave top-up, and a voluntary contribution to all three accounts. For an employee only the first two earn CPF Cash Top-up Relief. A contribution to all three accounts earns none and counts against the S$37,740 CPF Annual Limit. Sources: IRAS, "CPF Relief for employees"; CPF Board FAQ on the differences between topping up retirement savings, MediSave and the three CPF accounts. The research file marks this confirmed (verify2-topup.json, vc3a-no-relief), and a search this audit agreed.
findings.consequence: An employee on S$6,500 a month plus S$13,000 bonus has about S$4,070 of Annual Limit room. If she follows "Put S$8,000 into your CPF" by choosing the three-accounts option, S$4,070 is accepted with no relief. About S$285 of the promised saving is gone and the money is spread across her three accounts for good. On S$60,000 a year the whole S$8,000 can go the wrong way (S$560 at 7%).
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the "No relief for" cell and the workbook note at planner.ts:325: "Voluntary contributions to all three CPF accounts. In the CPF app choose the retirement top-up (Special or Retirement Account) or the MediSave top-up, not 'contribute to my three CPF accounts'." Change the headline wording to "into your CPF Special/Retirement or MediSave Account as a cash top-up". Change warnings.ts:216 to "Voluntary contributions to your three CPF accounts do not earn relief; a cash top-up to MediSave is counted under CPF top-up, self."

findings.where: src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:72-83 (hint shown only after Foreigner is picked) and 182-192 (months worked); src/web/text.ts:479-480, 514; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:165-172; workbook/sheets/start.ts:100, 106; SPEC.md section 6.11 (no warning code for this)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: The only guidance is "A foreigner who is a Singapore tax resident for the year. Non-residents are taxed differently and are not covered." (web, after choosing Foreigner) and "For Singapore tax residents only." (workbook). Nowhere is "tax resident" explained, and there is no warning when a foreigner enters six months of work or fewer.
findings.what_is_true: A foreigner is tax resident for a Year of Assessment if they stayed or worked in Singapore at least 183 days in the calendar year before it. IRAS also treats as resident a foreigner whose employment straddles two calendar years for 183 days in a row, and one holding a work pass valid for at least a year (reviewed at tax clearance). A non-resident gets no personal reliefs, pays 15% or the resident rates on employment income, whichever is higher, and gets no SRS relief. Sources: IRAS, "Working out my tax residency" and "Individual income tax rates" (research file: tax-resident-def and non-resident, both confirmed); IRAS, "SRS contributions" (srs-foreigner-relief, confirmed).
findings.consequence: Engine run: a foreigner who started in August 2026, five months at S$12,000. The tool shows tax of S$1,880 and recommends S$19,000 into SRS "saving S$1,330", with no warning. If she leaves before reaching 183 days she is a non-resident. Her tax is 15% of S$60,000, which is S$9,000. The S$19,000 earns no relief, and getting it back costs tax on the whole amount plus the 5% penalty.
findings.suggested_fix: Put one line under Residency for all three choices, and in the workbook note at planner.ts:170: "Tax resident means you lived or worked in Singapore for at least 183 days in the income year (IRAS has extra rules for stays that run across two years)." Add a caution when residency is Foreigner and months worked is 6 or fewer: "You worked here for under 183 days this year. You are a tax resident only if your stay continues into next year to reach 183 days in a row, or your work pass runs for at least a year and you stay. Otherwise you pay 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher, with no reliefs, and an SRS contribution earns you nothing. Check with IRAS first."

findings.where: workbook/sheets/planner.ts:290, 314, 472; workbook/sheets/start.ts:107-109; workbook/sheets/scenarios.ts:115-116; compare src/web/text.ts:380-472 (the web page's "What locking the money away means" table)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: The paid workbook says of SRS only: "Locked until retirement age; early withdrawals are taxed with a 5% penalty." It labels the saving "Tax saved ÷ cash locked away: an immediate return." It lists "tax on SRS withdrawals in retirement" among things not covered. It describes family recipients as "parents, grandparents, in-laws, or a low-income spouse or sibling". No sheet says that half of every SRS withdrawal is taxable, which retirement age applies, when CPF money comes back, the S$8,000 income test, or the matched-top-up rule beyond one line on the Start sheet.
findings.what_is_true: The free web page states all of this correctly (SPEC section 5.4): half of each SRS withdrawal at retirement age is taxable; the retirement age is 62, 63 or 64 by date of first contribution; CPF top-ups come back only as payouts; a spouse or sibling qualifies only if they earned no more than S$8,000 in the year before the top-up or have a disability; matched top-ups and CPF transfers earn nothing. The underlying rules are confirmed in the research file (srs-withdrawal, retirement-age, topup-family, topup-exclusions).
findings.consequence: A buyer of the S$19.90 workbook sees "an immediate return" of 11.5% on S$15,300 of SRS and is never told the withdrawals are taxed later. Another buyer tops up S$8,000 for a wife who earned S$20,000 last year, reading "low-income" as covering her, and gets no relief: S$920 at 11.5%.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a "Before you transfer" block in the workbook from the same lock-up facts text the web page uses (Start sheet, or under the Planner results). Change the note at planner.ts:472 to "Tax saved this year ÷ cash locked away. For SRS, half of what you later withdraw is taxable." Change planner.ts:290 to "...or a spouse or sibling who earned no more than S$8,000 in the year before the top-up, or has a disability."

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:494-497 (fifth bullet of "Check before you move money"); workbook/sheets/start.ts:107; SPEC.md section 6.4 lines 352-355
findings.claim_or_behaviour: "If you have unused Parenthood Tax Rebate, you will pay less tax this year than shown here. The saving from this plan arrives later, when the rebate would otherwise have run out." In the workbook this appears only on the Start sheet, not beside the result.
findings.what_is_true: The Parenthood Tax Rebate (S$5,000, S$10,000 or S$20,000 per child) is set against tax payable and carries forward. While it covers the whole bill, a year-end contribution saves no cash that year. The benefit arrives only if and when the rebate runs out, which can be years away, or never if the parent stops working. Source: IRAS, "Parenthood Tax Rebate" (research file: ptr, confirmed). The spec puts the balance out of scope; the problem is where and how firmly the user is told.
findings.consequence: Engine run: a mother of 34 on the example income with S$12,000 of child reliefs and S$10,000 of unused rebate. The headline says "You save S$2,603" for locking away S$23,300 by 31 December. Her bill of S$5,834 is S$0 either way this year. Many advisers would tell her to wait until the year the rebate runs out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a tick-box "I have unused Parenthood Tax Rebate" (no amount needed). When ticked, show a caution under the headline and in the workbook's "Things to check": "With unused Parenthood Tax Rebate your tax bill for this year may already be S$0. This plan would then save nothing now; it only makes the rebate last longer. Consider waiting until the year the rebate runs out."

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:60 and 212 (label "Worth it (7%+)"), 401-403 ("Locked until"); src/web/state.ts:25; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:360-378; SPEC.md section 8.3 line 586
findings.claim_or_behaviour: The default minimum of 7 cents per dollar is labelled "Worth it (7%+)" for every user. The CPF lock-up is described as "You can start CPF payouts. The money becomes part of your monthly retirement payouts (CPF LIFE)." No age or number of years is given.
findings.what_is_true: A cash top-up to the Special Account cannot be taken out at 55 or used for housing. It is paid as monthly payouts from the payout eligibility age of 65. An SRS account first funded now is locked to 64. Source: CPF Board, "Top up to enjoy higher retirement payouts" and "What is the CPF LIFE payout age?" (verified this audit from search extracts). Whether 7 cents once is worth a 35-year lock-up is a judgement, not a rule; the default order (SRS first) is defensible.
findings.consequence: Engine run: a 28-year-old on S$6,500 a month plus S$13,000 bonus. The default plan locks away S$23,300 (S$15,300 until 64, S$8,000 until 65, so 36 to 37 years) to save S$1,631 once. The page calls that "Worth it" and never states the years.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the option to the neutral "7 cents or more". Add a line to the recommendation card worked out from the age, for example "SRS locked until 64 (36 years). CPF comes back as monthly payouts from 65 (37 years)." Change text.ts:402 to "From 65, as monthly payouts (CPF LIFE). It cannot be withdrawn at 55 or used for housing."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "MediSave: up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (S$79,000)." For family: "The same limits, measured on the family member's accounts." The caution says "Log in to CPF to see how far each account is from the Full Retirement Sum and the Basic Healthcare Sum."
findings.what_is_true: S$79,000 applies to members aged 65 or under in 2026. The Basic Healthcare Sum is fixed for life in the year a member turns 65 (S$75,500 for those who turned 65 in 2025, lower for older cohorts). A parent's Retirement Account also accepts top-ups above the Full Retirement Sum with no relief. The giver cannot log in to a parent's CPF. Source: CPF Board, "What is the Basic Healthcare Sum" (research file: verify2-topup.json checker notes, confirmed).
findings.consequence: A daughter plans S$8,000 into her 70-year-old mother's MediSave using the S$79,000 figure. The mother's own limit is lower, so the excess is refunded and the relief shrinks unless she redirects the money before 31 December. A top-up to a father whose Retirement Account is already above the Full Retirement Sum is accepted and earns nothing: S$920 at 11.5% on S$8,000.
findings.suggested_fix: Change text.ts:439 to "MediSave: up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (S$79,000 if aged 65 or under in 2026; older members keep the lower figure set when they turned 65)." Change the family cell to "The same limits on their accounts. You cannot see them: ask your family member to check their CPF Retirement Dashboard for the top-up that still earns relief."

findings.where: src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:281-317 ("Already contributed"); src/web/text.ts:456, 517; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:268-291; SPEC.md section 1 line 51
findings.claim_or_behaviour: "Already contributed in 2026" asks for SRS and CPF top-ups with no hint about employer payments. "Employer SRS contributions" appears only under "What this does not model". SRS "Who qualifies" reads: "Age 18 or over, not an undischarged bankrupt, and a tax resident for YA2027."
findings.what_is_true: An employer's SRS contribution is taxable pay and earns the employee SRS relief; that it shares the employee's yearly cap is my understanding, and the research file could not confirm it. An employer's cash top-up to the employee's CPF counts towards the employee's own S$8,000 (IRAS: top-ups "made by you or your employer"). No SRS contribution is allowed after a withdrawal made at or after the prescribed retirement age (IRAS SRS declaration form). A foreigner must file a yearly declaration with the SRS bank to get the S$35,700 cap. Sources: IRAS, "SRS contributions" and "CPF Cash Top-up Relief" (search extracts this audit; research file srs-employer, employer-topup, srs-foreigner-relief).
findings.consequence: If the shared cap holds, an employee whose employer paid S$6,000 into her SRS is told to put in S$15,300; the bank takes only S$9,300 and the saving is overstated by S$690 at 11.5%. A 64-year-old who has started SRS withdrawals is told to contribute S$15,300 that the bank will refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hint under "Already contributed": "Include anything your employer paid into your SRS or topped up to your CPF in cash; it counts towards the same limits. Add employer SRS payments to your pay as well." Extend the SRS "Who qualifies" cell: "...and you have not started withdrawing at retirement age. Foreigners must give their SRS bank a declaration each year to use the S$35,700 cap."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "Never includes a wasted dollar." (workbook Scenarios sheet) and "Never recommends a wasted dollar." (README and spec).
findings.what_is_true: The tool avoids dollars it can see are wasted: above the S$80,000 cap, above a scheme cap, or against tax-free income. It cannot see CPF balances, matching grants, a family member's eligibility or tax residency. Findings F2 to F5 are cases where a recommended dollar earns no relief.
findings.consequence: A buyer who reads an absolute promise and then gets no relief on a matched or over-limit top-up (S$230 to S$1,020 in the examples above) has a fair complaint against the seller.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to "Never includes a dollar it can see would be wasted. It cannot see your CPF balances, matching grants or a family member's eligibility: check those first."

findings.where: src/engine/rules/shared.ts:87-96 (Working Mother's Child Relief), 98-114 (Parent Relief), 139-145 (Grandparent Caregiver Relief)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: Working Mother's Child Relief help: "Children born or adopted from 1 Jan 2024: S$8,000 (1st), S$10,000 (2nd), S$12,000 (3rd onwards). Children born earlier: 15% / 20% / 25% of your earned income. Enter the total." Parent Relief help: "S$9,000 per dependent parent ... Up to 2 dependants in total."
findings.what_is_true: The amounts are right. Three conditions that change the figure are missing. First, Qualifying Child Relief plus Working Mother's Child Relief is capped at S$50,000 per child, the child must be a Singapore Citizen, and total Working Mother's Child Relief cannot exceed the mother's earned income. Second, Parent Relief is per dependant, not per claimant: siblings supporting the same parent share one S$9,000 or S$5,500. Third, Grandparent Caregiver Relief is one S$3,000 claim and needs a caregiver who is not working. Source: IRAS relief pages (research file: verify2-reliefs.json, wmcr, parent and grandparent-caregiver checker notes).
findings.consequence: Two siblings who each enter S$9,000 for the same mother overstate their reliefs by S$9,000 between them. For the one who cannot claim, tax is understated by S$1,035 at 11.5% and the plan may stop S$9,000 too early.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the help texts. Working Mother's Child Relief: "Singapore Citizen children only. With Qualifying Child Relief it cannot exceed S$50,000 per child." Parent Relief: "The amount is per parent, shared between everyone who claims for that parent." Grandparent Caregiver Relief: "One claim of S$3,000; the caregiver must not be working."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "A spouse or sibling counts only if they earned no more than S$8,000 last year or have a disability."
findings.what_is_true: The test year is the year before the year of the top-up, so 2025 income for a 2026 top-up. "Last year" reads wrongly when the user is planning income year 2027 or looking back at 2025. Source: IRAS, "CPF Cash Top-up Relief" (research file: topup-family, confirmed).
findings.consequence: A user planning 2027 top-ups in the projected year may test the wrong year's income for a spouse who stopped working in 2026.
findings.suggested_fix: Fill the year from the rules: "...only if they earned no more than S$8,000 in 2025 (the year before the top-up) or have a disability."

checked_and_fine: Resident tax brackets from YA2024 and the cumulative tax at each boundary, used for all three income years.
No Personal Income Tax Rebate is applied for YA2026 or YA2027, and the YA2025 rebate (60%, capped at S$200) is correctly excluded; a search this audit found no rebate for YA2026.
The no-rebate assumption for YA2027 is shown under Sources, Assumptions on the web page and on the workbook Rules sheet.
The S$80,000 cap covers CPF relief, Earned Income Relief, SRS, top-up relief and other reliefs; donations (at 250%) and employment expenses come off before reliefs, in the right order.
Earned Income Relief of S$1,000 / S$6,000 / S$8,000 by age on 31 December of the income year, limited to earned income; disability amounts of S$4,000 / S$10,000 / S$12,000 offered as the difference.
CPF Ordinary Wage ceiling of S$7,400 (2025) and S$8,000 (2026, 2027), the S$102,000 annual ceiling, the Additional Wage ceiling formula and the S$20,400 maximum employee contribution.
CPF employee and employer rates for 2025, 2026 and 2027 in all five age bands, including the 1 January 2026 and 1 January 2027 senior-worker increases.
First- and second-year PR graduated rates, the S$500 to S$750 phase-in, and the rounding rule.
The CPF rate change from the month after the 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday, in both the formula and the birth-month prompt.
Only compulsory employee CPF counts as CPF relief; the override is capped at the yearly maximum.
SRS caps of S$15,300 (Citizen/PR) and S$35,700 (foreigner), minimum age 18, the bankruptcy and tax-resident conditions, and the 31 December deadline with a bank cut-off warning.
SRS retirement age of 62 / 63 / 64 by date of first contribution, the 5% penalty with full taxation on early withdrawal, and 50% taxable over 10 years with S$40,000 a year tax-free for a resident.
No SRS rule change for 2026 or 2027 was found in a search of MOF and IRAS this audit.
CPF Cash Top-up Relief caps: S$8,000 for self (Special or Retirement Account and MediSave share it) plus S$8,000 for family.
The giver of a family top-up must be a Citizen or PR (confirmed by search this audit), and the family lever is correctly withheld from foreigners.
The family recipient list, the S$8,000 income test for a spouse or sibling in the year before the top-up, and the disability exception (web wording).
Cash only for top-up relief, with the Full Retirement Sum and Basic Healthcare Sum limits stated; the matched-top-up exclusions from 2025 and 2026 are stated, though without amounts (see F2).
MediSave top-ups are limited by the Basic Healthcare Sum and not by the CPF Annual Limit since 2022 (confirmed by search), so the tool is right not to apply the Annual Limit.
Full Retirement Sum, Enhanced Retirement Sum and Basic Healthcare Sum for 2025, 2026 and 2027; the 2027 Basic Healthcare Sum is flagged as a placeholder.
Relief catalogue amounts: Spouse S$2,000 / S$5,500; Qualifying Child S$4,000; Child (Disability) S$7,500; Working Mother's Child Relief S$8,000 / S$10,000 / S$12,000 and 15% / 20% / 25%.
Relief catalogue amounts: Parent S$9,000 / S$5,500 and S$14,000 / S$10,000; Sibling (Disability) S$5,500; Grandparent Caregiver S$3,000; NSman S$1,500 / S$3,000 / S$3,500 / S$5,000 and S$750.
Life Insurance Relief's S$5,000 CPF test, and the removal of Course Fees Relief (from YA2026) and Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Relief (from YA2025).
"Foreigner (tax resident)" and "non-resident" are kept distinct in the wording; foreigners get no CPF relief or CPF top-up lever.
Income year 2027 is flagged as projected wherever it is shown; the 250% donation deduction is carried to 2029 as the research file corrected it.
Recommending SRS before CPF top-ups by default is defensible: SRS keeps a penalised exit and CPF top-ups are irreversible, and the page says so.
At the 2% and 3.5% brackets nothing is recommended by default, and the offer to go further shows the true cents per dollar.
Self-employed income, the Not Ordinarily Resident scheme, foreign income and non-residents are listed as not modelled on the web page, the workbook Start sheet and the README.

Employer CPF figures, the full-employer/graduated-employee option for new PRs, and the second-year PR rate above age 65, which the research file also left unread.
